questions.text: What is a method in Java?
options: A block of code that only runs when called
questions.hint: Methods are reusable blocks of code that perform specific tasks.

questions.text: Which keyword is used to define a method that belongs to the class itself?
questions.hint: Think about the difference between class-level and object-level methods.

questions.text: How do you call a static method named 'myMethod' from the class 'MyClass'?
questions.hint: Static methods belong to the class, not an instance.

questions.text: What is required to call an instance (non-static) method?
options: Nothing, it can be called directly
questions.hint: Instance methods belong to objects.

questions.text: Static methods can access instance variables directly without creating an object.
questions.hint: Think about what 'static' means in the context of class members.

questions.text: What is the name of the method that is automatically called when an object is created?
questions.hint: It shares the same name as the class.

questions.text: Which access modifier provides the highest level of visibility?
questions.hint: This modifier allows access from anywhere in the project.

questions.text: Which access modifier restricts access to only within the same class?
questions.hint: This is the most restrictive level of access.

questions.text: What is the visibility of a member with no explicit access modifier (default)?
options: Within the same package and by subclasses
questions.hint: This is also known as 'package-private'.

questions.text: Which modifier allows access within the same package and by subclasses in different packages?
questions.hint: Think about the 'franchise recipe' analogy.

questions.text: A public member of a class can be accessed from any other class in the project.
questions.hint: 'Public' is the 'menu board' accessible to everyone.

questions.text: According to the 'rule of thumb' for access modifiers, you should pick the _____ level that still gets the job done.
questions.hint: It's easier to widen access later than to restrict it.
Which method call is missing a required reference?

questions.text: In the 'zones' analogy, which zone corresponds to 'private' access?
questions.hint: It's the innermost, most restricted zone.

questions.text: A 'protected' member is accessible to any class in the same package.
questions.hint: Protected access includes both package-level access and subclass access.

questions.text: The keyword used to indicate a method does not return a value.
questions.hint: It's a commonly used method return type.

questions.text: What is the purpose of the 'return' statement in a method?
options: To print a value to the console
To exit the method and optionally pass back a value
questions.hint: It controls the flow of the program and sends data back.

questions.text: Which access modifier would you use for a constant (like 'Math.PI') that needs to be accessed from anywhere?
questions.hint: These are often 'world-level' for maximum accessibility.

questions.text: Which modifier is often described as the 'house blend, shared among staff on shift'?
questions.hint: Think about visibility within the same package only.

questions.text: A 'private' member of a class can be accessed by a method in the same class.
questions.hint: Check the visibility matrix for the 'private' access level.

questions.text: What is the term for data that is passed into a method to be used within it?
questions.hint: They are defined in the method's parentheses.
Encapsulation involves hiding internal data.

questions.text: A protected member is always accessible outside its package.
questions.hint: Protected access depends on the relationship between classes.

questions.text: What is the benefit of using methods in programming?
options: They make the code longer and more complex
They allow for code reuse and organization
They prevent the use of variables
They are only used for mathematical operations
questions.hint: Think about the 'write once, call anywhere' principle.

questions.text: In the 'Visibility Matrix', which access level offers the most restricted access?
questions.hint: The 'personal notebook' analogy is key.

questions.text: In the real-life analogy, the 'menu board' corresponds to which access modifier?
questions.hint: Think about what is visible to everyone walking in.

questions.text: Why is it considered a best practice to keep fields (instance variables) private?
options: To enforce encapsulation and control access via methods
To prevent the class from being inherited
questions.hint: This is a core principle of Object-Oriented Programming.

questions.text: A static method can call an instance method directly without an object.
questions.hint: Static methods can only access other static members directly.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct order of access modifiers from most restrictive to least restrictive?
questions.hint: Refer to the 'Visibility Matrix' or the list of modifiers in the lesson.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is true regarding encapsulation?
options: It uses public fields to allow free access to data.
It is achieved by making fields private and providing public getters/setters.
It allows objects to inherit methods from their superclass.
It is solely about making methods public.
questions.hint: Encapsulation is about protecting data and controlling access.
